tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list image projects accessible to the connected Imagelato account and retrieve identifiers for subsequent project operations. Returns each project's id and name, 25 per page by default. Not for a project's processed images.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read metadata for one Imagelato image project selected by its exact name or identifier. Returns its id, name, logo URL and created and edited times, or not-found. Not for a quick look at its latest processed images.

tools.name: add_project
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to create one Imagelato image project to group processed batches and resize presets. Returns the new project's id, name and creation time and fires the project.created webhook. Each call creates another project. Not for adding a resize preset.

tools.name: list_batches
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list existing processed-image batch metadata in Imagelato, optionally scoped to a project. Returns each batch's id, slug, output format and template id, 25 per page by default. Not for one batch's variant files and links.

tools.name: get_batch
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read the output metadata and first-party file links for one existing Imagelato processed-image batch. tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to list existing Imagelato resize and format presets, optionally scoped to one project. Returns each template's id, name, project, output formats and pixel widths, 25 per page by default. Not for the images processed with them.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to read one Imagelato resize preset selected by its exact name or identifier. Returns its project, output formats, pixel widths and created and edited times, or not-found. Not for changing it.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_project, get_batch, list_team_members · Private data: list_batches, get_batch, delete_batch, open_imagelato · Public sink: add_project, delete_batch, update_template, list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_batches, get_batch, delete_batch, list_templates, update_template, show_project_overview.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_project, get_batch, list_team_members · Private data: list_batches, get_batch, delete_batch, open_imagelato · Public sink: add_project, delete_batch, update_template, list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_batches, get_batch, delete_batch, list_templates, update_template, show_project_overview

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
